summary: Isso is a self-hosted comment server (a Disqus alternative): a Python WSGI app backed by SQLite that stores threads, comments with a moderation/approval state machine and rate-limited voting, and a runtime preferences table (used as the signing key source).

tools.description: Post a new comment on a thread, addressed by its page URI. The thread must already exist (create it with thread_create first). Optionally reply to an existing comment by passing its id. Comments are created queued for moderation and become publicly visible only once approved (see comment_approve).

uri.description: URI of the thread to comment on.

email.description: Email address (kept for notifications; never shown publicly).

website.description: A URL for the commenter, rendered as a link.

parent.description: Id of the published comment this is a reply to. Omit for a top-level comment.

title.description: Thread title, used only when the thread is first created by this call.

messages.precondition: Create the thread for this URI before commenting (see thread_create).
messages.fk: That thread could not be found.
messages.fk_missing: The thread for this URI must be created first.
messages.not_found: The thread for this URI does not exist.

tools.description: Fetch the published comments of a thread, addressed by its page URI: the root comment id, the total and hidden reply counts, and the list of published comments. Queued and deleted comments are not shown. Optionally restrict to one root comment's replies, filter by creation time, and control depth.

uri.description: URI of the thread to fetch.

parent.description: If set, return only replies to this root comment.

after.description: Only comments created after this unix timestamp.

limit.description: Maximum number of root-level comments to return.

nested_limit.description: Maximum depth of nested replies to expand.

sort.description: Order of replies: newest, oldest, or upvotes.

offset.description: Pagination offset into the root comments.

plain.description: If true, return raw text; otherwise render markdown.

messages.not_found: The thread for this URI does not exist.

tools.description: Edit a comment's text, author, or website by id. Cannot change the comment's thread, parent, or voting fields.

tools.description: Delete a comment by id, supplied together with the signed edit cookie that proves ownership. A comment that has replies cannot be deleted directly — delete its replies first. Once deleted, the comment row is removed entirely (leaf comments) and its notifications are cleared.

Only a comment that is still in the moderation queue can be approved; an already-published comment is left unchanged.

messages.precondition: Only a comment that is still in the moderation queue can be approved.
messages.transition: That comment is not in the moderation queue, so it cannot be approved.

remote_addr.description: Voter address used for deduplication. Omit to let it be taken from the session.

tools.description: Stop receiving reply notifications on a comment, using the signed unsubscribe token that was emailed to the subscriber. The token must decode to the exact email being unsubscribed; the comment's notification flag is turned off so no further reply emails are sent.

id.description: Id of the comment to unsubscribe from.

email.description: Email address that is being unsubscribed.

key.description: Signed unsubscribe token (from the unsubscribe link in a notification email).

messages.precondition: That comment does not exist, so there is nothing to unsubscribe from.

_evidence.entity_why: primary effect row_update lands on this table
_evidence.ref_code:
def unsubscribe(self, environ, request, id, email, key):
    email = unquote(email)
    rv = self.isso.unsign(key, max_age=2**32)
    ...
    if rv[0] != "unsubscribe" or rv[1] != email:
        raise Forbidden
    item = self.comments.get(id)
    if item is None:
        raise NotFound
    with self.isso.lock:
        self.comments.unsubscribe(email, id)
